title: Henselization of pairs commutes with filtered colimits
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a directed set and $(A_\lambda,I_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ a directed system of pairs: commutative rings $A_\lambda$ with ideals $I_\lambda$ and ring maps $\varphi_{\mu\lambda}:A_\mu\to A_\lambda$ for $\mu\le\lambda$ (compatible, $\varphi_{\lambda\lambda}=\mathrm{id}$) with $\varphi_{\mu\lambda}(I_\mu)\subseteq I_\lambda$. Let $A=\varinjlim_\lambda A_\lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] with coprojections $\alpha_\lambda:A_\lambda\to A$, and let $I=\bigcup_\lambda\alpha_\lambda(I_\lambda)$ (an ideal of $A$, the colimit of the $I_\lambda$). For every $\lambda$ let $(A_\lambda^h,I_\lambda^h)$, $I_\lambda^h=I_\lambda A_\lambda^h$, be the henselization of $(A_\lambda,I_\lambda)$ [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization]. Then: (1) for $\mu\le\lambda$ there is exactly one ring map $\varphi^h_{\mu\lambda}:A_\mu^h\to A_\lambda^h$ with $\varphi^h_{\mu\lambda}\circ(A_\mu\to A_\mu^h)=(A_\lambda\to A_\lambda^h)\circ\varphi_{\mu\lambda}$, so that $(A^h_\lambda,I^h_\lambda)$ is a directed system of pairs; (2) let $A^h_\infty=\varinjlim_\lambda A^h_\lambda$ (colimit of rings along the $\varphi^h_{\mu\lambda}$) with coprojections $\iota_\lambda$, $I^h_\infty=\varinjlim_\lambda I^h_\lambda=\bigcup_\lambda\iota_\lambda(I^h_\lambda)$, and $\eta_\infty:A\to A^h_\infty$ the ring map with $\eta_\infty\circ\alpha_\lambda=\iota_\lambda\circ(A_\lambda\to A_\lambda^h)$ for all $\lambda$; then $(A^h_\infty,I^h_\infty)$ is the henselization of $(A,I)$: if $\eta:A\to A^h$ is the henselization of $(A,I)$ [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization], there is exactly one ring map $u:A^h_\infty\to A^h$ with $u\circ\eta_\infty=\eta$, it is an isomorphism, and $u(I^h_\infty)=IA^h$. In particular, if $(A,I)$ is a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], then for every $\lambda$ there is exactly one ring map $\beta_\lambda:A_\lambda^h\to A$ with $\beta_\lambda\circ(A_\lambda\to A_\lambda^h)=\alpha_\lambda$; it maps $I_\lambda^h$ into $I$, the $\beta_\lambda$ are compatible with the $\varphi^h_{\mu\lambda}$, and they induce an isomorphism $\varinjlim_\lambda A_\lambda^h\cong A$ under which $\varinjlim_\lambda I^h_\lambda$ corresponds to $I$.

The ring map $\eta_\lambda\circ\varphi_{\mu\lambda}:A_\mu	o A^h_\lambda$ maps $I_\mu$ into $\eta_\lambda(I_\lambda)\subseteq I_\lambda A^h_\lambda=I^h_\lambda$, and $(A^h_\lambda,I^h_\lambda)$ is henselian, so by [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-universal-property] (applied to $(B,J)=(A_\mu,I_\mu)$, $(A',I')=(A^h_\lambda,I^h_\lambda)$) there is exactly one ring map $\varphi^h_{\mu\lambda}:A^h_\mu	o A^h_\lambda$ with $\varphi^h_{\mu\lambda}\circ\eta_\mu=\eta_\lambda\circ\varphi_{\mu\lambda}$, and $\varphi^h_{\mu\lambda}(I^h_\mu)\subseteq I^h_\lambda$. proof.text: *The colimit pair $(A^h_\infty,I^h_\infty)$ is henselian.* The colimit $A^h_\infty=\varinjlim_\lambda A^h_\lambda$ of the directed system of step 1 exists in commutative rings (a directed set is a filtered category; the filtered colimit is the disjoint union of the $A^h_\lambda$ modulo the evident relation, with operations computed at a common later index) [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise]; let $\iota_\lambda:A^h_\lambda\to A^h_\infty$ be the coprojections, and $I^h_\infty=\bigcup_\lambda\iota_\lambda(I^h_\lambda)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-henselian-pair], applied to the directed system of henselian pairs $(A^h_\lambda,I^h_\lambda)$ of step 1, $I^h_\infty$ is an ideal of $A^h_\infty$ and $(A^h_\infty,I^h_\infty)$ is a henselian pair. The family $\iota_\lambda\circ\eta_\lambda:A_\lambda\to A^h_\infty$ is a cocone on $(A_\lambda)$: for $\mu\le\lambda$, $\iota_\lambda\circ\eta_\lambda\circ\varphi_{\mu\lambda}=\iota_\lambda\circ\varphi^h_{\mu\lambda}\circ\eta_\mu=\iota_\mu\circ\eta_\mu$. So there is exactly one ring map $\eta_\infty:A\to A^h_\infty$ with $\eta_\infty\circ\alpha_\lambda=\iota_\lambda\circ\eta_\lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. It maps $I=\bigcup_\lambda\alpha_\lambda(I_\lambda)$ into $I^h_\infty$: $\eta_\infty(\alpha_\lambda(x))=\iota_\lambda(\eta_\lambda(x))$ with $\eta_\lambda(x)\in I_\lambda A^h_\lambda=I^h_\lambda$ for $x\in I_\lambda$. (Stacks: 'Since the colimit is filtered we obtain $\colim(A_i^h,I_i^h)=(\colim A_i^h,\colim I_i^h)$ in the category of pairs; details omitted. Again using the colimit is filtered, this is a henselian pair'.)

proof.text: *(2) The comparison maps $u$ and $v$.* Let $\eta:A\to A^h$ be the henselization of $(A,I)$; $(A^h,IA^h)$ is henselian [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization] (2). For each $\lambda$, $\eta\circ\alpha_\lambda:A_\lambda\to A^h$ maps $I_\lambda$ into $\eta(I)\subseteq IA^h$, so [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-universal-property] gives exactly one $u_\lambda:A^h_\lambda\to A^h$ with $u_\lambda\circ\eta_\lambda=\eta\circ\alpha_\lambda$, and $u_\lambda(I^h_\lambda)\subseteq IA^h$. They form a cocone: for $\mu\le\lambda$, $u_\lambda\circ\varphi^h_{\mu\lambda}\circ\eta_\mu=u_\lambda\circ\eta_\lambda\circ\varphi_{\mu\lambda}=\eta\circ\alpha_\lambda\circ\varphi_{\mu\lambda}=\eta\circ\alpha_\mu=u_\mu\circ\eta_\mu$, so $u_\lambda\circ\varphi^h_{\mu\lambda}=u_\mu$ by the uniqueness clause. Let $u:A^h_\infty\to A^h$ be the induced map, $u\circ\iota_\lambda=u_\lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Then $u\circ\eta_\infty=\eta$, since both agree after every $\alpha_\lambda$ ($u\circ\eta_\infty\circ\alpha_\lambda=u_\lambda\circ\eta_\lambda=\eta\circ\alpha_\lambda$) and $A$ is the colimit; and $u$ is the only ring map with $u\circ\eta_\infty=\eta$: for any such $u'$, $u'\circ\iota_\lambda\circ\eta_\lambda=u'\circ\eta_\infty\circ\alpha_\lambda=\eta\circ\alpha_\lambda$, so $u'\circ\iota_\lambda=u_\lambda$ by uniqueness of $u_\lambda$, and $u'=u$ by the colimit property. Conversely, $(A^h_\infty,I^h_\infty)$ is henselian and $\eta_\infty(I)\subseteq I^h_\infty$ (step 2), so [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-universal-property] (for $(B,J)=(A,I)$) gives exactly one $v:A^h\to A^h_\infty$ with $v\circ\eta=\eta_\infty$, and $v(IA^h)\subseteq I^h_\infty$.

proof.text: *(2) $u$ and $v$ are inverse; the ideals.* $u\circ v\circ\eta=u\circ\eta_\infty=\eta=\mathrm{id}\circ\eta$, and $(A^h,IA^h)$ is henselian with $\eta(I)\subseteq IA^h$, so $u\circ v=\mathrm{id}_{A^h}$ by the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-universal-property] (for $(B,J)=(A,I)$, $(A',I')=(A^h,IA^h)$). For each $\lambda$: $v\circ u\circ\iota_\lambda\circ\eta_\lambda=v\circ\eta\circ\alpha_\lambda=\eta_\infty\circ\alpha_\lambda=\iota_\lambda\circ\eta_\lambda$; since $(A^h_\infty,I^h_\infty)$ is henselian and $\iota_\lambda\circ\eta_\lambda$ maps $I_\lambda$ into $I^h_\infty$, the uniqueness clause (for $(B,J)=(A_\lambda,I_\lambda)$) gives $v\circ u\circ\iota_\lambda=\iota_\lambda$; hence $v\circ u=\mathrm{id}$ by the uniqueness in the colimit property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. So $u$ is an isomorphism with inverse $v$. Ideals: $u(I^h_\infty)=\bigcup_\lambda u_\lambda(I^h_\lambda)\subseteq IA^h$ (step 3) and $v(IA^h)\subseteq I^h_\infty$, i.e. $IA^h\subseteq u(I^h_\infty)$; so $u(I^h_\infty)=IA^h$. This proves clause (2). (Stacks: 'Hence by the Yoneda lemma we find $(A^h,I^h)=(\colim A_i^h,\colim I_i^h)$'.)

proof.text: *The case $(A,I)$ henselian.* Assume $(A,I)$ henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. For each $\lambda$, $\alpha_\lambda$ maps $I_\lambda$ into $I$, so [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-universal-property] (for $(B,J)=(A_\lambda,I_\lambda)$, $(A',I')=(A,I)$) gives exactly one ring map $\beta_\lambda:A^h_\lambda\to A$ with $\beta_\lambda\circ\eta_\lambda=\alpha_\lambda$, and $\beta_\lambda(I^h_\lambda)\subseteq I$. Compatibility: for $\mu\le\lambda$, $\beta_\lambda\circ\varphi^h_{\mu\lambda}\circ\eta_\mu=\beta_\lambda\circ\eta_\lambda\circ\varphi_{\mu\lambda}=\alpha_\lambda\circ\varphi_{\mu\lambda}=\alpha_\mu$, so $\beta_\lambda\circ\varphi^h_{\mu\lambda}=\beta_\mu$ by uniqueness. Let $\beta:A^h_\infty\to A$ be the induced map, $\beta\circ\iota_\lambda=\beta_\lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Then $\beta\circ\eta_\infty\circ\alpha_\lambda=\beta_\lambda\circ\eta_\lambda=\alpha_\lambda$ for all $\lambda$, so $\beta\circ\eta_\infty=\mathrm{id}_A$. And $\eta_\infty\circ\beta\circ\iota_\lambda\circ\eta_\lambda=\eta_\infty\circ\alpha_\lambda=\iota_\lambda\circ\eta_\lambda$, where both $\eta_\infty\circ\beta\circ\iota_\lambda$ and $\iota_\lambda$ are ring maps $A^h_\lambda\to A^h_\infty$ and $(A^h_\infty,I^h_\infty)$ is henselian with $\iota_\lambda\eta_\lambda(I_\lambda)\subseteq I^h_\infty$ (step 2); by the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-universal-property], $\eta_\infty\circ\beta\circ\iota_\lambda=\iota_\lambda$ for all $\lambda$, hence $\eta_\infty\circ\beta=\mathrm{id}$. So $\beta$ is an isomorphism $\varinjlim A^h_\lambda\cong A$ with inverse $\eta_\infty$. Ideals: $\beta(I^h_\infty)=\bigcup_\lambda\beta_\lambda(I^h_\lambda)\subseteq I$, and $\eta_\infty(I)\subseteq I^h_\infty$ (step 2), i.e. $I\subseteq\beta(I^h_\infty)$; so $\beta(I^h_\infty)=I$. (This argument does not use $A^h$; equivalently it is clause (2) together with $A^h\cong A$ for a henselian $(A,I)$.)

lean.statement: theorem pairHenselization_colimit {Λ : Type u} [Preorder Λ] [IsDirected Λ (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty Λ] (F G : Λ ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (η : F ⟶ G) (J : ∀ i : Λ, Ideal (F.obj i)) (hJ : ∀ {i j : Λ} (f : i ⟶ j), Ideal.map (F.map f).hom (J i) ≤ J j) (hG : ∀ i : Λ, ∃ c : Cocone (ObjectProperty.ι (fun C : Under (F.obj i) ↦ AlgebraicGeometry.Etale (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map C.hom) ∧ Function.Bijective (Ideal.quotientMap ((J i).map C.hom.hom) C.hom.hom (Ideal.le_comap_map)))), Nonempty (IsColimit c) ∧ ∃ e : c.pt.right ≅ G.obj i, c.pt.hom ≫ e.hom = η.app i) (c : Cocone F) (hc : IsColimit c) (I : Ideal c.pt) (hI : ∀ x : c.pt, x ∈ I ↔ ∃ (i : Λ) (a : F.obj i), (c.ι.app i).hom a = x ∧ a ∈ J i) (d : Cocone G) (hd : IsColimit d) : ∃ Ih : Ideal d.pt, (∀ x : d.pt, x ∈ Ih ↔ ∃ (i : Λ) (a : G.obj i), (d.ι.app i).hom a = x ∧ a ∈ (J i).map (η.app i).hom) ∧ ∃ ηInf : c.pt ⟶ d.pt, (∀ i : Λ, c.ι.app i ≫ ηInf = η.app i ≫ d.ι.app i) ∧ (∀ (A : CommRingCat.{u}) (ζ : c.pt ⟶ A), (∃ ch : Cocone (ObjectProperty.ι (fun C : Under c.pt ↦ AlgebraicGeometry.Etale (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map C.hom) ∧ Function.Bijective (Ideal.quotientMap (I.map C.hom.hom) C.hom.hom (Ideal.le_comap_map)))), Nonempty (IsColimit ch) ∧ ∃ e : ch.pt.right ≅ A, ch.pt.hom ≫ e.hom = ζ) → (∃! u : d.pt ⟶ A, ηInf ≫ u = ζ) ∧ (∀ u : d.pt ⟶ A, ηInf ≫ u = ζ → Function.Bijective u.hom ∧ Ideal.map u.hom Ih = I.map ζ.hom)) ∧ (HenselianRing c.pt I → ∃ β : ∀ i : Λ, G.obj i ⟶ c.pt, (∀ i : Λ, η.app i ≫ β i = c.ι.app i ∧ (∀ b : G.obj i ⟶ c.pt, η.app i ≫ b = c.ι.app i → b = β i) ∧ Ideal.map (β i).hom ((J i).map (η.app i).hom) ≤ I) ∧ (∀ {i j : Λ} (f : i ⟶ j), G.map f ≫ β j = β i) ∧ ∃ b : d.pt ⟶ c.pt, (∀ i : Λ, d.ι.app i ≫ b = β i) ∧ Function.Bijective b.hom ∧ Ideal.map b.hom Ih = I)
